3. Defendant Nos. 8 and 9, 11-15 opposed the application for injunction contending, inter anti, that the plaintiffs have no title and possession in the suit land. It has been further contended in the written objection that defendant Nos. 9-15 have title and possession over 3 decimals of land in suit plot No. 86 in which their homestead stands and the said land has also been duly recorded in their names in the RS Khatian and they have been paying rent regularly to the appropriate authority. It has been further contended that defendant No. 9 has already constructed a pucca building in suit plot No. 86 and there are other structures standing thereon and the said land is well fenced by walls on all four sides and under such circumstances there is absolutely no ground for granting temporary injunction on vague and indefinite assertions of the plaintiffs. 

 4. The learned Subordinate Judge by the impugned order dated 17-7-94 found that the plaintiffs have failed to make out a prima facie case in support of their claim for temporary injunction. The learned Subordinate Judge on consideration of the materials on record also found that there is nothing on record to prima facie prove that the plaintiffs have possession in suit plot No. 86. On the other hand, the constesting defendants have produced the certified copies of the finally published RS Khatian in which 26 decimals of land has been recorded in their names. From the DCR and the rent receipts produced by the contesting defendant if is found that they have been paying rent to the appropriate authority for the said land. RAJUK has already approved their plan for construction of buildings in the said land. It has been clearly asserted in the written objection that the construction of the building has already been finished. Suit plot No. 86 admittedly measures 32 decimals of land in which the contesting defendants appear to have possession over 20 decimals of land. The plaintiffs alleged claim of 10 decimals of land in this particular part is totally vague and indefinite. In such circumstances, the learned Subordinate Judge found that the plaintiffs have failed to make out a prima facie case for injunction. From the facts and circumstances of the case and materials on record we find that the learned Subordinate Judge was perfectly justified in refusing the plaintiffs'' prayer for temporary injunction. We find no illegality in the impugned order calling for our interference.
